item.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Putin says US plan ‘could form basis’ of ceasefire deal
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated a revised US peace proposal could be a foundation for an agreement, provided Ukraine withdraws troops from Moscow-claimed territories. He warned of forceful acquisition if Kyiv refuses. Ukraine has firmly rejected any territorial concessions, with President Zelensky's aide emphasizing no land will be surrendered as long as he leads.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: National Guard troop shot near White House dies; second victim critical, Trump says
item.description: Tragedy struck near the White House as a National Guard soldier, Sarah Beckstrom, succumbed to injuries from a shooting. President Trump announced her death, stating the second soldier is critically wounded. The alleged attacker, an Afghan national with prior CIA ties, is also injured and will face severe repercussions. The incident prompted lockdowns of nearby federal buildings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why some long-time YouTube channels are disappearing without warning
item.description: Established YouTube channels are vanishing overnight due to aggressive AI moderation, falsely flagging them for spam or deceptive practices. Creators report these automated systems, lacking human review, are causing significant disruption and financial harm. Many channels are only restored after public outcry, highlighting a critical flaw in YouTube's current safety framework and prompting calls for regulatory oversight.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Who was Fuzzy Zoeller? Famous two-time major champion golfer dies at 74 after Masters history
item.description: Golf legend Fuzzy Zoeller, the last player to win the Masters on his debut in 1979 and a 1984 U.S. Open champion, has passed away at 74. Known for his personality and memorable moments, Zoeller's career also included a notable controversy in 1997. He leaves behind a legacy of significant wins and sportsmanship.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: 'You have a criminal record': Indian-origin Sikh man stopped from entering Canada from US, interaction goes viral
item.description: An Indian-origin Sikh man, claiming US citizenship, was denied entry into Canada by a border officer due to a prior criminal record. The man accused the officer of religious discrimination, but the officer explained the decision was based on Canadian databases and laws, not his religion or origin. The video of the interaction that the man recorded went viral.

item.title: Hasan Pikar calls out Asmongold for ‘Hasan is finished’ video over China trip clips
item.description: Hasan Piker has refuted Asmongold's claim that he is "finished" following backlash over his China trip content. Piker argues that Asmongold exaggerated minimal criticism from his community, including concerns about horse racing, into a narrative of widespread cancellation. The exchange highlights how reaction videos can amplify isolated incidents into larger controversies.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: How Rahmanullah Lakanwal made it from Afghanistan to US before White House shooting — Inside Operation Allies Welcome
item.description: Operation Allies Welcome, a federal initiative meant to aid Afghans escaping the Taliban, finds itself in a troubling spotlight following a shooting incident that injured two National Guard members. Investigations reveal that the program has been marred by substantial data inaccuracies and lack of thorough oversight, raising concerns over the vetting process.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Canadian company buys UK’s most iconic Indian restaurants, including Veeraswamy and Chutney Mary
item.description: Canadian firm Fairfax Financial Holdings has acquired MW Eat Ltd, which owns iconic Indian restaurants like Michelin-starred Veeraswamy. The acquisition comes as Veeraswamy's owners are in a legal battle with The Crown Estate over a lease renewal dispute. The original founders will continue working with Fairfax to expand the restaurant group globally.
item.dc:creator: NAOMI CANTON

item.title: US CEO backs H-1B, says $100,000 fee will hurt economy: 'Immigrant workers have different skill sets'
item.description: International Bank of Commerce CEO Dennis Nixon championed for the H-1B visa, calling the proposed $100,000 fee 'prohibitive' for entrepreneurs. He argued that while large corporations can absorb the cost, it will stifle innovation by limiting foreign talent access for smaller ventures. The CEO said America's ageing population can't fill the skill gap.

item.title: Candace Owens raises new questions as she seeks footage of Egyptians she claims came to Provo before Charlie Kirk’s death
item.description: Candace Owens claims a new break in the Charlie Kirk death case, alleging a group she calls "Egyptians" booked hotel rooms in Orem, Utah, days before Kirk's demise. She urged locals to check cameras for footage from September 4-13, 2025, but has provided no proof for her claims. Authorities have not confirmed these allegations.

item.title: ‘A long fight’: Southeast Asia battles with widespread flooding; over 80 dead in Thailand, hundreds missing in Sumatra
item.description: Southern Thailand's severe flooding has claimed over 80 lives, impacting millions across 12 provinces. Rescue efforts are ongoing, with drones and helicopters aiding stranded residents. Neighboring Indonesia and Malaysia are also grappling with deadly floods and landslides, with hundreds missing in Sumatra.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Nuclear race: Putin warns to be ‘ready for any development’, says can discuss stability with US
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has directed officials to prepare for potential nuclear weapons tests, a move not seen since the Soviet era. This directive follows US President Trump's announcement of resuming nuclear testing. Russia also expressed readiness to discuss strategic stability with the United States amidst deteriorating bilateral relations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hong Kong fire tragedy: Toll rises to 75, flames still visible on Day 2; 3 suspects held for manslaughter
item.description: A devastating fire at a Hong Kong housing complex has claimed 65 lives, with hundreds still missing. The blaze, believed to have started in scaffolding, engulfed seven of eight towers. Three men have been arrested for manslaughter amid a corruption probe into the renovation project, as authorities investigate fire-resistance standards and consider phasing out bamboo scaffolding.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Desi MAGA backer: Who is Nalin Haley? Son of Indian-origin ex-US ambassador taking on Vivek Ramaswamy
item.description: Nalin Haley, son of Nikki Haley, has publicly criticized Vivek Ramaswamy's childcare proposals, calling them "third world parenting style." Haley, who advocates for strict immigration policies and has faced scrutiny over his own loyalty, is increasingly vocal on the right. This online spat highlights a growing divide within conservative politics.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Was Kyle Divine arrested? Strong rumors rise as KaizenDIYGym influencer faces troubling stepdaughter accusations
item.description: Online fitness personality Kyle Divine faces serious allegations after a viral Instagram post detailed a chat with a sexual violence hotline. His 16-year-old stepdaughter reportedly claimed abuse and drug provision. Divine was arrested on November 26 for contributing to the delinquency of a minor and child seduction, with his court date set for December 2, 2025.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta
